newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cathay confident about future prospects.
newsitem.headline: Cathay confident about future prospects.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd said on Wednesday it was optimistic about its future prospects and confident that its revenue strategy would cushion any adverse impacts of yen movements.
"We face the future from a position of considerable strength," chairman Peter Sutch said in a statement.
"I believe we have the resources to ensure Cathay Pacific enters the new century as a world-class, customer-driven airline producing superior financial returns," he said.
The Hong Kong flag carrier earlier posted a 27.9 percent rise in 1996 net profit to HK$3.81 billion.
Analysts estimates for attributable profits ranged from HK$3.7 billion to HK$4.0 billion.
Cathay Pacific said increasing cost pressures and declining yields in most markets had required constant attention.
"The effects of adverse exchange rates and spiraling fuel prices were also cause for concern during the year," it said.
The weakening of the yen caused a fall-off in revenues from northeast Asian markets that was only partially offset by an increase in passenger traffic, it added.
"While it is out of our hands, we will be watching the performance of the yen closely in 1997. However, I'm confident our revenue strategy will cushion any adverse effect," said Sutch.
He said Hong Kong's new Chek Lap Kok airport presented opportunities and hoped these would not be undermined by "excessive landing charges or associated fees".
"The move to the new airport will be a welcome relief from the congestion and capacity constraints of Kai Tak airport although it is expected to bring increases in our operational cost," said Sutch.
